field_strength_detail.note: Strokes per round vs an average PGA Tour player (DataGolf-style scale). Reference only: prices use the field-relative number (mu averages 0 over the field).

course_data.label: course length only (no course fit or history this week)
course_data.note: Course fit and course history are blank for every player this week, so the model cannot tell who suits this course. The only course term is a general adjustment for course length and par.

form_source.scale: adjusted strokes gained a round vs an average PGA Tour field

divergence.method: Presentation only; prices are unchanged. Odd one out: mean log-odds gaps over the win/top 10/top 20 markets all three sources price; two sources agree within 0.15, the odd one out is 1.8x further from both. Data Golf check: logit(DG chance) on DG's re-centred skill number across the field, per market; flagged when our skill-number gap with DG and our chance-based gap (in DG strokes) differ by 0.35+, DG's rating misses its chances by 0.2+ (next market agreeing) and the player has a 5%+ top-20 chance. Gap vs the sportsbooks: the shape skill gap read against the closest-priced players (up to 3 cheaper and 3 dearer within 0.35 win log-odds): how far we rate the player from them vs how far the sportsbooks do, and which adjustment groups make our difference.

finish.calibration_note: exact tapes ranked with random tie-break vs the run's probabilities (dead-heat rules differ slightly)

edge_model.note: edge_sg = (model - market) in strokes per round via the model's own logit slope per market. attribution = ridge share of that gap loading on each field-relative component: a statistical attribution, not causal
